_note: Seed 3 rolls a Thief Pickpocket Human — a normal (non-Troll/Elven/Dwarven) race so priceFor's multipliers don't complicate the arithmetic, and a class that can legally buy every weapon/armor slot openStore might roll. The test bumps state.c.gold to 5000 identically on BOTH the prototype and engine sides right after boot (before opening the store) so the scenario can afford a full spread of purchase categories (food/potion/weapon/armor/premium/lockpicks) and still land on a genuine insufficient-gold case at the end — openStore itself is deterministic from the seed, so this gold bump changes nothing about which stock rolls, only what's affordable. 'openStore'/'buyItem'/'leaveStore' indices below were hand-verified against this exact seed's rolled stock (see test/parity/economy-parity.test.js's harness note). A top-level `divergence` record (kind action-path, fromAction 0, stockCostMul 1.25) is declared for this fixture's Pickpocket hero (Phase 24, IDENT-05/FID-07): the store roll is proven byte-identical to the prototype while gold, weapon, and items diverge because every routed store line costs 1.25x more, making the Set-of-lockpicks and Katana purchases (actions 6-7) unaffordable on the engine side two purchases before the prototype runs dry.

divergence.rationale: The seed-3 hero is a Human Pickpocket; Phase 24 marks up every priceFor-routed store line (buyWeapon/buyArmor/buyPremium/buyRations/repairArmor) x1.25 for a Pickpocket, floor 1. Phase 39 (GEAR-01) re-prices the WEAPONS table itself, so a flat multiplier off the PROTOTYPE's own cost no longer describes the engine's line prices (the prototype is frozen at Katana 525/Axe 50/Broadsword-premium 500; the engine now sells Katana 650, Broadsword 550, before the 1.25x Pickpocket markup) — the stockCostMul check is replaced by the stronger stockNames/stockAfter pin: the store ROLL is still byte-identical to the prototype (same 12 names, in order — Rations is the engine's own extra line, excluded from stockNames and present only in stockAfter) while every routed cost is measured directly. With the same 5000-gold bump on both sides, the higher engine prices no longer starve the run the way the old prices did: the engine now affords everything the prototype does PLUS extra purchases the prototype's own gold ran out before reaching (the fixture's own action order buys Axe/Studded/Casket/Lockpicks/Katana/Speed potion in sequence) — action 5 (Casket, 4128) still fails on both sides (both are far short of a ~4100-gold premium item at this point), but the engine ends the script with 2066 gold left over (vs the prototype's 55) and a Speed potion the prototype could never reach. `weaponUpgradeDelta`'s expected-strike heuristic still makes the Axe purchase (action 3) NOT an upgrade over the Pickpocket's starting Dagger (which already out-crits a bare Axe) — but Phase 61 (STORE-02) changes what happens to a legal, not-better store buy: it is charged and BAGGED (`deliverGear` -> `stowItem` + `purchaseBagged`) rather than charged and discarded (the frozen prototype's own behaviour, and this engine's pre-Phase-61 behaviour, both of which paid for the Axe and threw it away via takeItem's `notBetter` rejection branch). Gold is charged identically either way (end gold 2066, unchanged by this phase) — the ONLY field this phase moves is `after.items`, where the Axe now appears between the Healing potion and the Lockpicks. Measured directly by `tools/worn-fixture-scan.mjs` and a live replay (test/parity/divergence-records.test.js's `STORE-02 (Phase 61)` guard). Seed/actions/gold bump are deliberately untouched — the divergence is declared, not dodged. Purchase mechanics parity for a non-Pickpocket hero is unchanged code (buyFrom/takeItem/sellItem's arithmetic paths are untouched for a non-Pickpocket sub) and is covered instead by test/unit/economy.test.js's priceFor/sellPriceFor/seed-3-stock-pin cases. Phase 39 (GEAR-05, Plan 04) appends two MORE engine-only lines after Rations — this seed-3 hero starts with neither a Rope nor a Torch, so at depth 1 (tier 0) both are offered flat-priced (no priceFor route, so the Pickpocket markup never applies to them either): Torch 25, Rope 60 (no Ladder — tier 1+ only). Both are stripped from stockNames (ENGINE_ONLY_STORE_EFFECTS, mirroring Rations) and measured directly in stockAfter, same as every other engine-only line; the fixture's action-path fields (gold/weapon/items) are unaffected since the script never buys either. Phase 43 (CLAR-01 HP-not-WP sweep): the engine's Healing potion txt unit is hp; the prototype's stays wp — a cosmetic, declared, measured field. Phase 45 (HEDGE-01/03, 2026-09-19): newRun now wears the Thief's starting cloak at chargen (c.worn.cloak), so the end-state's engine items list loses it (bought items stay bagged) and c.worn is populated; the store visit never wears/unwears anything itself, so end.after.worn is unchanged from chargen; measured by tools/worn-fixture-scan.mjs (BEFORE readout committed in 45-01).

floorFeatureShift.rationale: USER RULING D/G (Phase 54-07 fit, BAND-02, 2026-09-21): ENCOUNTER_DOTS fitted to { base: 7, perDepth: 0.3 } (from identity { base: 9, perDepth: 1 }) changes difficultyCurve(depth).dots — genFloor's feature-scatter loop (engine/maze.js) walks the SAME rng.shuffle(far) result but assigns the first dots array slots to the 'dot' feat before moving on to tele/chest/trap/climb/gorge, so a smaller dots count shifts every later feature category's starting index by the same delta, remapping which cells land on which feat — the rng cursor itself is UNCHANGED (the shuffle runs once regardless of dots; nothing after it draws more or fewer times), so this is a pure, deterministic re-mapping, not new randomness. This scenario never navigates the maze (combat/casting starts immediately at chargen), so only the BOOT floor (depth 1) is measured. Measured live via newRun(seed) vs the frozen prototype sandbox, never hand-typed.
